Reframed assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- Policy stance remains distinctly dovish and growth-supportive: ELB (0–0.25 percent), average inflation targeting that tolerates inflation moderately above 2 percent, and continued large-scale asset purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B MBS), with supportive operational tools (repo, ON RRP, reinvestments).
- Financial conditions remain accommodative, aiding the flow of credit to households and businesses.
- SLOOS corroborates improving credit intermediation: large banks eased standards across several mortgage categories (GSE-eligible, QM jumbo, QM non-jumbo non-GSE), and foreign banks reported strengthened demand for C&I loans. These trends are consistent with an improving outlook and better market functioning.
- That said, SLOOS also notes ongoing caution: banks continue to cite concerns around the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and risk tolerance; conditions for smaller firms appear uneven. These align with broader vulnerabilities flagged elsewhere and keep the system sensitive to shocks.
- Net: The SLOOS tilts the balance modestly more positive versus a policy- and FSR-only read, reflecting gradually improving credit supply and demand, but lingering bank-reported concerns warrant continued caution.

Revised slightly higher to reflect SLOOS-implied easing and demand improvement.
